scope: Theorem 3.1 (Initial estimates) of the manuscript “An Almost-Linear Approximation Scheme for Edit Distance” (preprints/An-Almost-Linear-Approximation-Scheme-for-Edit-Distance-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 121 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 7ecda63faaa7d6a3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 9. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: With the parameters and labeled interval tree of Section 2, there is a lazily evaluated random table U(0)(I, q) of integers in [0, N] such that, with probability at least 0.99, simultaneously at every state, c(I, q) ≤ U(0) (I, q) ≤ Ainitc(I, q). (3.1) Every zero-cost state has value zero on every execution. Conditional on any first request for an entry and the previously exposed randomness, its expected evaluation cost is at most (1 + |I|)2o(H), uniformly in the state. This cost bound includes arithmetic and random sampling and does not require (3.1) to hold.
